speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help understand your symptoms, do you have any history of autoimmune diseases or recent exposure to new medications or supplements? Also, have you noticed any darkening of your urine or lightening of your stools?

speaker: Patient
text: 32-year-old male. The patient reports a 2-month history of increasing generalized fatigue and severe pruritus. He has known hypertension and was diagnosed with ulcerative colitis 5 years ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and inconsistent condom use.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of ulcerative colitis, I suspect a liver complication, so I will request a Chest X-ray to rule out other causes and check for autoimmune markers. REQUEST TEST: Antimitochondrial Antibody (AMA) Test

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the AMA is negative, I need to check for antibodies associated with Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis, which is strongly linked to your ulcerative colitis. REQUEST TEST: Antinuclear Antibody (ANA) Test

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the autoimmune markers are negative, I need to evaluate for infectious causes like Hepatitis given your sexual history, as well as visualize the bile ducts to rule out Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis despite the normal p-ANCA. REQUEST TEST: Hepatitis B and C Serology, MRCP

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the negative autoimmune and infectious workup, I need to assess for other causes of cholestasis and liver injury. Have you noticed any jaundice, right upper quadrant pain, or changes in your appetite? REQUEST TEST: Liver Biopsy

speaker: Doctor
text: It is highly unusual for a liver biopsy to be completely normal in the context of significant cholestasis and pruritus. Could you clarify if you have noticed any pale stools or dark urine, and have you recently started any new over-the-counter medications or herbal supplements? REQUEST TEST: Serum IgG4, Lipid Panel

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Serum IgG4: 180 mg/dL, Total Cholesterol: 320 mg/dL, Triglycerides: 180 mg/dL

speaker: Doctor
text: The elevated IgG4 and severe hypercholesterolemia with cholestasis strongly suggest IgG4-related sclerosing cholangitis. I will request imaging to visualize the characteristic bile duct strictures. REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Generalized fatigue and severe pruritus. I also have Scleral icterus, Multiple scratch marks on trunk and extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of scleral icterus confirms jaundice, which aligns with the cholestatic pattern and elevated IgG4 levels. Given the strong association with ulcerative colitis and the specific lab findings, I will finalize my assessment. DIAGNOSIS READY: IgG4-related sclerosing cholangitis
